heading: Questions, answered.
description: Everything you need to know about Helix and how it orchestrates atomic work-breakdown for AI coding agents.

items.question: What is Helix, in one sentence?
items.answer: Helix is an atomic work-breakdown orchestrator for AI coding agents — it decomposes every prompt into reviewable units, executes them in dependency order, and verifies each one against your repo before opening a PR.

items.question: How is it different from running an agent directly in my IDE?
items.answer: An in-IDE agent produces one sprawling diff. Helix produces many small, reviewable PRs — each scoped to a single atomic unit — so code review stays fast and regressions stay local.

items.question: Which AI models does Helix support?
items.answer: Helix is model-agnostic. Bring any coding-agent capable of running shell commands and reading diffs — the orchestrator handles decomposition, dependency gating, and verification around the model.

items.question: Can I self-host Helix?
items.answer: Yes. Helix is MIT licensed. The orchestrator runs as a Node.js process; the dashboard is the Next.js marketing + control-plane site you are looking at right now.

items.question: Does Helix send my code anywhere?
items.answer: Only to the model provider you configure. Helix itself has no telemetry and no required cloud account — set the provider API key and you're done.

items.question: How do I deploy this site to Vercel?
items.answer: From the repo root, run `vercel` for a preview deploy and `vercel --prod` for production. The included `vercel.json` pins framework, region, and security headers automatically.
